cues.text: The little wren
Manuel Francisco dos Santos was born in 1933 in Pau Grande, a small town in the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
His family was poor and large.
He was born with bent legs, and his right leg was six centimetres shorter than his left.
When he was a child, one doctor wrote that he was disabled.
He was also smaller than other children, so his sister called him Garrincha.
A garrincha is a little brown bird, a wren.
Let the little bird fly.
The name stuck.
Being different is not a weakness. The things that make you different can become your strength.
Waiting for a chance
At fourteen, Garrincha worked in a cloth factory and played for his town’s team.
But the coach, Carlos Pinto, would not let him play in matches.
He thought Garrincha was too young, and he worried about the strong defenders on other teams.
Garrincha got tired of waiting.
He signed up with Serrano, a team in the nearby city of Petrópolis, and played there for almost a year.
Swing the factory gate open.
After that, Carlos Pinto finally gave him his chance, on the right wing.
Waiting is hard. Keep practising, and remember that finding another place to grow is not giving up.
Two clubs said no
Garrincha’s games caught the eye of Arati, a former Botafogo player, who took him to the club.
Before that, two other clubs, Vasco and São Cristóvão, had turned him down.
At his first training session with Botafogo, Garrincha dribbled past Nílton Santos, a famous Brazil defender, and even put the ball through his legs.
Nílton was so impressed that he asked the club to sign him.
Lift the flap to see who spoke up.
On 19 July 1953, Garrincha scored three goals in his first game for the team.
Hearing no can hurt. Keep going, because one person who believes in you can change everything.
Left out
In his first years at Botafogo, some people said Garrincha dribbled too much.
Brazil had other good players in his position, and he was not picked for the 1954 World Cup squad.
Garrincha kept playing his own way for Botafogo.
Flip the scoreboard.
In 1957 he scored 20 goals in 26 games, and Botafogo won the Rio state championship, the Campeonato Carioca.
That helped convince the selectors to pick him for the 1958 World Cup in Sweden.
Being left out hurts. You can keep working hard and still be true to yourself.
A test and a chance
Before the 1958 World Cup, the team’s psychologist gave the players a drawing test.
Garrincha scored low, and the psychologist said taking him to the World Cup would be a mistake.
In Sweden, he was left out of Brazil’s first two matches.
In the third match, against the Soviet Union, he finally played.
Brazil started so brilliantly that people call it the best three minutes of football of all time.
Unfold the pitch.
In the final, Garrincha set up two goals, and Brazil won its first World Cup.
A test can’t measure everything about you. Stay ready, because your chance can still come.
The Joy of the People
At the 1962 World Cup in Chile, Brazil’s young star Pelé was injured after the second match.
Garrincha stepped up to lead his team.
He scored four goals, two against England and two against the hosts, Chile.
Brazil beat Czechoslovakia 3–1 in the final and won the World Cup again.
Garrincha was named the best player of the tournament.
Raise the banner.
Brazilians called him the Joy of the People, and the Bent-Legged Angel.
The boy with bent legs became one of the greatest dribblers of all time.
What makes you different can bring joy to other people. Be proud of who you are.
